hooks.command:
# Find the repository from the session, then hand off to the script that owns the
# rest. Two candidates, in order of trustworthiness. If neither resolves, SAY SO —
# a session-end step that skips in silence is how a dashboard goes stale without a
# word. Always exit 0: a missed sync is recoverable, a failed session end is not.
for d in "${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-}" "$(git -C "$PWD" rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)"; do
  [ -x "$d/scripts/dashboard-sync.sh" ] && exec "$d/scripts/dashboard-sync.sh"
done
printf '%s  SKIPPED — no governed repository found (CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR=%s, PWD=%s), so scripts/dashboard-sync.sh never ran. Dashboard NOT synced.\n' \
  "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" "${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-unset}" "$PWD" \
  >> "$HOME/.claude/session-end-sync.log" 2>&1
exit 0

# Per-turn dashboard sync. Same script as SessionEnd, with --turn, which makes it
# quiet on the no-op path — it runs after every assistant turn, so a line per turn
# saying "nothing new" would drown the log it writes to.
#
# $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR is fixed when the session starts and goes stale if the
# repository moves mid-session. The script re-derives the root from its own
# location regardless; this only has to find the script.
#
# Always exits 0. A missed sync costs one `npm run sync`; a Stop hook that exits
# non-zero blocks the turn, which is not recoverable by the person waiting for it.
for d in "${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-}" "$(git -C "$PWD" rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)"; do
  [ -x "$d/scripts/dashboard-sync.sh" ] && exec "$d/scripts/dashboard-sync.sh" --turn
done
exit 0

# Publish a ledger entry the moment it is written, not when the turn ends.
# The Stop hook fires once per USER turn, and the usual shape of work is one user message,
# reserve an entry, then do the job — so exactly one sync ran, at the end, and an entry was
# never visible while it was in flight. Reserving is a file write, so this triggers on file
# writes. Guarded by one `find` over ledger/*.md: milliseconds when nothing there changed,
# which is what makes it safe after every tool call. Always exits 0.
for d in "${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-}" "$(git -C "$PWD" rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)"; do
  [ -x "$d/scripts/ledger-sync-guard.sh" ] && exec "$d/scripts/ledger-sync-guard.sh"
done
exit 0
